outcome: vaginal delivery rates after successful ECV
cohort: The study participants were 51,002 patients with singleton live births in the USA who underwent documented external cephalic version between 2010 and 2014.
finding: Maternal morbid obesity is associated with a decreased success rate of external cephalic version (ECV) and lower rates of vaginal delivery even after a successful ECV.
mod_finding: Women with higher BMI had a decreased rate of vaginal delivery after successful ECV compared to those with normal BMI (59.5% vs 81.0%).
